subject: ACME POC kickoff - scope & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC kickoff - scope & next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today — good to meet the ACME team. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps to get the POC scoped and started. Please reply with any corrections.

1) Pain points (as discussed)
- Search/embedding latency frequently >300ms at peak and causing poor UX.
- Per-query inference cost spikes when batch sizes are small; unpredictable unit economics.
- Model output variability on our long-form generative prompts (hallucinations for product descriptions).

2) Top-level goals for the POC
- Reduce embedding median latency to <150ms and embedding cost per 10k requests by ~40%.
- Improve generative output quality for product-description prompt set (target precision uptick measured via eval set).
- Validate integration flow for both search and a chat assistant (end-to-end).

3) Proposed POC scope (6 weeks)
- Endpoints: embeddings (search), chat/generation (customer support), reranking test harness, and a logging/observability route.
- Prompt sets & evals: ~50 embedding test queries, 20 gen prompts with labeled quality markers (we'll run automated evals).
- Success metrics: embedding p95 latency, embedding cost per 10k ops, gen quality delta on labeled evals, and integration stability (uptime/5xx rate).

4) Owners
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, program lead), Rishi Malhotra (Solutions Eng, infra & quantization), Aditya Rao (SE, integration & eval harness).
- ACME: John Smith (Product lead), Priya Shah (Engineering lead), ACME Eng team (eng-team@acme.com).

5) Timeline / milestones
- Week of Jun 21: Tech sync + access exchange (credentials, allowlist).
- Week of Jun 28: Environment setup + baseline runs.
- Week of Jul 12: Mid-point review + tuning/quantization experiments.
- Week of Jul 26: Final evaluation & handoff / next steps.

6) Access & setup checklist (what we need from ACME)
- Short-term: a test dataset (CSV or S3 path), an allowlisted IP or AWS role for Redwood to send test traffic, and a service account/api key for initial integration testing.
- Security: SOC2 questionnaire in progress — we'll share a scoped evidence list if needed.

Attachments: redwood-poc-sow.pdf (SOW + milestones), acme-access-worksheet.xlsx (access fields we need).

Immediate next steps
- Can you confirm the Week of Jun 28 kickoff window?
- Please share initial credentials or the contact who will provision them by Jun 25.
- I'll schedule a 60-min technical kick-off with Rishi/Aditya included — propose Tue Jun 22 10:00 AM PT unless that conflicts.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Marissa — thanks for the summary and for pulling that together so quickly. Confirming the list is accurate from our discussion. A couple of quick notes: 

- Pain points: yes — latency and cost are the headline issues. Also call out that our nightly reindex job is currently a bottleneck; interested to see if caching/batching helps.
- Timeline: Week of Jun 28 works for the kickoff.

Action items from our side:
- I'll have Priya (cc'd) own the provisioning and she will share the service account details by EOD Friday Jun 25.
- Technical contact for env access is eng-team@acme.com — they will also set the allowlist.

We are excited to see what Redwood can do here. Please go ahead and schedule the tech sync for Tue Jun 22 10:00 AM PT; that time works for me.

—John

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC kickoff - scope & next steps

Great — thanks John and Priya. I scheduled the tech sync for Tue Jun 22 10:00 AM PT and sent a calendar invite to everyone on the thread. Agenda for the 60-min tech sync:

- 10m Introductions & outcomes
- 15m ACME infra & access details (Priya / eng-team)
- 20m Redwood baseline plan (Rishi) — runtime, batching, caching approach + model variants
- 10m Eval & prompt set review (Aditya) — we will walk through the 50 embedding queries and 20 gen prompts
- 5m Next steps & owners

Prompt set / evals: I uploaded the initial prompt lists and the eval harness to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-redwood-acme-poc (view only for now). Please let us know which prompts you want to exclude or add before the kickoff.

Pre-kick items for Redwood (what we'll prepare before Jun 28)
- Baseline runs on a small sample (Rishi) and an initial quantization plan.
- Eval harness populated with ACME prompt sets (Aditya).
- Temporary API key for ACME dev env with allowlist restrictions (Marissa to coordinate).

If you run into provisioning delays, let me know and we can run local stubs to keep momentum. See HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/ACME-2027-POC-001.

Thanks — see you on Tue.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME POC prep checklist

Quick internal note before the tech sync — want to make sure we're aligned on pre-kick prep: \

- Rishi: please prepare baseline perf runs (embedding p50/p95, token throughput) and a short quantization recommendation (Q4_8 vs Q5_4 tradeoffs) we can share in the sync.
- Aditya: populate the eval harness with the 50 embedding queries + 20 gen prompts and add expected labels where available. Also include the reranking scenario we discussed.
- Marissa (me): I'll follow up with Priya for provisioning and confirm calendar invites.

Goal: have the baseline report and eval harness ready by EOD Jun 25 so we can run a quick verification before Jun 28.

Thanks — M.
